title: Separable Rank of Radial Kernels in Two and Higher Dimensions: Machine-Checked Proofs in Lean 4 and Isabelle/HOL
abstract: A d-variate kernel K : X_0 x ... x X_{d-1} -> K has separable rank at most N if it is a sum of N coordinatewise products sum_{n=0}^{N-1} prod_{j=0}^{d-1} f_{n,j}(x_j). On a d-dimensional Cartesian grid of support width L, a rank-R kernel evaluates in d R L one-dimensional taps per grid point rather than L^d. While a positive Gaussian exp(-alpha ||x||^2) has separable rank 1, approximating flat-top or oscillatory isotropic kernels---such as defocus disks, Airy point-spread functions, circular low-pass filters, or band-limited wave propagators---with finite coordinatewise separable rank relies on signed or oscillatory profiles built from complex-rate Gaussians and exponential polynomials. We give a complete machine-checked characterization in Lean 4 (with Mathlib) of the d-way separable rank of continuous circularly and spherically symmetric kernels K(x) = phi(||x||^2) on R^d for all d >= 2: (1) separableRank(K) < infinity over R if and only if phi agrees on [0, infinity) with a well-formed exponential-polynomial representation sum_i Re(P_i(s) exp(lambda_i s)) (nonzero polynomials P_i, distinct rates lambda_i with Im(lambda_i) >= 0, and real coefficients when Im(lambda_i) = 0); (2) over C, a continuous radial profile psi(||x||^2) has exact d-way separable rank sum_{mu in S} ((d - 1) deg P_mu + 1) for nonzero polynomials P_mu at distinct rates; (3) over R, every well-formed pure multi-Gaussian representation (deg P_i = 0) with r real rates and c nonreal upper-half-plane rates has exact d-way separable rank r + d c, achieved via an alternating 2d-th root-of-unity identity that splits each complex Gaussian into d real d-way products rather than 2^{d-1}, with optimality proved by Alder-Strassen rank substitution (showing in particular that scalar extension R -> C strictly lowers d-way rank when d >= 3); and (4) in d = 2, scalar extension preserves rank for arbitrary polynomial degrees, yielding exact real rank sum_i c_2(P_i, lambda_i) equal to the degree of the minimal monic constant-coefficient half-line differential annihilator p(D) phi_C = 0 (p in C[X]). Necessity reduces to showing that a continuous one-parameter semigroup M : [0, infinity) -> A is an exponential M(t) = exp(t A). Alongside the 96-line Banach-algebra integral-smoothing proof used in the main development, we formalize four finite-dimensional alternatives---one by finite differences in Lean 4 and three by Euler's infinitesimal step in Lean 4 and Isabelle/HOL using a homogeneous common-scale normalization eta = eps + ||M(eps) - 1|| that avoids any a priori difference-quotient bound---and compare their lengths, abstractions, and generality. Finally, we connect the 2d-th root-of-unity identity to two-dimensional harmonic ("beach-ball") differential operators and derive continuous-domain separable ranks and pass-count bounds for steerable derivative filter banks and three-dimensional isotropic propagators. Formalization: https://github.com/OlliNiemitalo/kernel-rank-lean
